To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the degree centrality of a node in a weighted network is the sum of the weights of its incoming ties; (ii) the betweenness centrality of a weighted network node is the sum of its incoming ties' weights multiplied by the fraction of shortest paths between all pairs of nodes that pass through it; and (iii) the closeness centrality of a weighed network node is the reciprocal of the sum of its outgoing ties' weights.
the proposed generalizations are better than existing ones, and that the generalizations that include both tie strength and tie number are better than those that include only tie strength.
the generalizations of degree, closeness and betweenness centrality proposed in this article are better measures of node centrability than their original and weighted counterparts.
